about: Links this machine to its Nerve centers.

common.about: Which center, when more than one is paired
common.name: --center <CENTER>

global.about: Where node.toml and the keys live [env: NERVE_CONFIG_DIR] [default: ~/.config/nerve, or /etc/nerve when installed as a service]
global.name: --config-dir <CONFIG_DIR>

global.about: Where the control socket and the audit log live [env: NERVE_STATE_DIR] [default: ~/.local/state/nerve, or /var/lib/nerve/state when installed as a service]
global.name: --state-dir <STATE_DIR>

global.about: Print JSON for programs instead of text: the read commands their data, the others the lines they print, an error {"error": ...}
global.name: --json

sections.about: Run the node as a service under a user of its own (Linux with sudo, Windows as administrator), set it up, keep it current, and back it up or move it.

verbs.about: Install the node as a service that starts with the machine and runs under a user of its own, make the account nerve-run for its commands and take you as the owner (Linux with sudo from your own account, Windows as administrator)

args.about: Run by root itself (Linux): `root` makes root the owner, so that user mode, and allowlist mode as the owner, run commands as root, with every right on the machine and over Nerve; needs --accept-root-owner. At a terminal install asks instead, and an owner root confirmed before stays. `none` leaves the node without an owner, root or another
args.name: --owner <ACCOUNT>

args.about: Confirms --owner=root: you accept that nothing in Nerve holds those commands back
args.name: --accept-root-owner

verbs.name: install

verbs.about: Stop and remove the service, nerve-run and its entries on your folders, the node's user and the program; the config and state folders stay

args.about: Delete the config and state folders too: the keys, the pairings and the audit log
args.name: --purge

verbs.name: uninstall

cards.about: Start, stop or restart the installed service, or show its state
cards.name: service

verbs.about: Start the installed service; the owner needs no root or administrator for it
verbs.name: service start

verbs.about: Stop it: the node ends its links and runs nothing until it starts again, at the latest with the machine
verbs.name: service stop

verbs.about: Stop it and start it again, so the node takes every change in node.toml
verbs.name: service restart

verbs.about: Show whether the node is installed as a service, whether it runs, and the program it runs with its version
verbs.name: service status

verbs.about: Name the node, choose where it keeps its keys, pair the first center and choose its mode and folder, one question at a time
verbs.name: setup

verbs.about: Replace the installed program with the latest release and restart the service; config, keys and audit log stay

args.about: Take the new program from this file instead of downloading the latest release
args.name: --from <FILE>

verbs.name: update

shared_args.about: Read the passphrase from the first line of this file instead of asking
shared_args.name: --passphrase-file <FILE>

verbs.about: Write the config and the keys to a file that a passphrase protects, to keep or to move the node to another machine

args.about: The file to write. It is private to you (mode 0600)
args.name: <FILE>

args.about: Also take the keys that are in the system keyring into the file; without it they stay there and are left out
args.name: --include-keyring

args.about: Replace the file when it exists
args.name: --overwrite

verbs.name: backup

verbs.about: Put the config and keys of a backup in place of this node's. The node must not run

args.about: The backup file
args.name: <FILE>

args.about: Replace a node here that is not the one the backup is of
args.name: --replace

args.about: Keep the keys in `file` or in the system `keyring` here, whatever the backup's config says
args.name: --secret-storage <file|keyring>

args.about: Leave the proxy out of the restored config, with its password and header values; set it again on this machine
args.name: --without-proxy

verbs.name: restore

sections.name: Install and set up

sections.about: Link this machine to centers and choose how it reaches them.

cards.about: Pair this machine with centers and decide what each one may change
cards.name: center

verbs.about: Pair this machine with a center, using the pairing link it showed

args.about: The pairing link
args.name: <LINK>

args.about: Read the pairing link from the first line of stdin: it holds the pairing code, and never shows in the process list
args.name: --link-stdin

args.about: The name to use for the center here (the center's own name if left out)
args.name: --name <NAME>

args.about: Do not ask before pairing
args.name: --yes

verbs.name: center add

verbs.about: Forget a center and delete its key
verbs.name: center rm

verbs.about: List the paired centers and how they are set
verbs.name: center ls

verbs.about: Stop the link to a center until you resume it
verbs.name: center pause

verbs.about: Link to a paused center again
verbs.name: center resume

verbs.about: Give this machine a new key for a center; the center takes the old one for 7 more days. Needs the running node, linked to that center

args.about: End the 7 days now: the center takes only the new key from then on
args.name: --end-grace

verbs.name: center rotate-key

verbs.about: Let a center change its own rights on this machine, up to user mode and sudo, or take that right away

args.about: What to grant; only `settings` exists
args.name: <WHAT>

args.about: `off`, or `write`: the center may then set everything this machine lets it do
args.name: <VALUE>

verbs.name: center grant

cards.about: Choose the proxy the node uses to reach centers
cards.name: proxy

verbs.about: Reach centers through an HTTP proxy. Header values and a password are kept in the system keyring, never in node.toml; the installed node on Windows takes neither

args.about: The proxy, http://host:port, or http://user:password@host:port when it wants a login; https://... for another proxy reached over TLS; or the nerve://relay link a relay showed, which holds its address, pin and this node's token
args.name: <URL>

args.about: The pin of an https:// proxy's certificate (a relay's: `nerve-node relay ls` there shows it); without it the system's roots check it
args.name: --pin <PIN>

args.about: A header for the proxy, `Name: value`; can be given more than once. The value goes into the system keyring
args.name: --header <NAME: VALUE>

args.about: Read the proxy's password from the first line of stdin, for a URL with a user name and no password (http://user@host:port); it never shows in the process list
args.name: --password-stdin

args.about: Read headers from stdin, one `Name: value` a line, after the password with --password-stdin
args.name: --headers-stdin

verbs.name: proxy set

verbs.about: Reach centers directly again, and delete the proxy's values from the system keyring
verbs.name: proxy rm

verbs.about: Show the proxy that is set and the names of its headers, never their values
verbs.name: proxy ls

cards.about: Let nodes that cannot reach a center themselves reach this node's centers through it
cards.name: relay

verbs.about: Turn the relay on: listen for other nodes at ADDRESS, like 0.0.0.0:7490. A node reaches only this node's own https centers through it

args.about: The address and port to listen on, like 0.0.0.0:7490 or [::]:7490
args.name: <ADDRESS>

args.about: Tunnels at once, over every relayed node (16 unless set)
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.about: Tunnels at once of one relayed node (4 unless set)
args.name: --max-links-per-node <N>

args.about: Tunnels one relayed node may open a minute, every node alike (30 unless set; for a relay behind this one, use `relay set-limits <name>`)
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.name: relay set

verbs.about: Turn the relay off: stop listening and end every tunnel. The nodes and their tokens stay
verbs.name: relay off

verbs.about: Let a node use the relay: makes its token and shows it once, in a link the other node pastes. Without --center its tunnels may go to every https center of this node

args.about: The relayed node's name here, 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once. Without it, every one
args.name: --center <CENTER>

args.about: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (without it: the address the relay listens on, else this machine's host name)
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.name: relay add

verbs.about: Change which centers of this node a relayed node may reach; without --center, every one. Its tunnels to others end

args.about: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.name: relay set-centers

verbs.about: Give a relayed node limits of its own, in place of the relay's --max-links-per-node and --max-opens-per-minute: for a relay behind this one, which carries many nodes. A flag not given keeps that limit; without either flag, the relay's limits again

args.about: Its tunnels at once
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.about: The tunnels it may open a minute
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.name: relay set-limits

verbs.about: Give a relayed node a new token and end the tunnels of the old one; its centers and limits stay. Shows the token once, in a link the other node pastes

args.about: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (as for `relay add`)
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.name: relay token

verbs.about: Take a node's token away and end its tunnels
verbs.name: relay rm

verbs.about: Show the relay, the nodes that may use it and, on a running node, who is connected
verbs.name: relay ls

cards.about: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and make the tokens that log in to it (the installed node on Linux; off unless turned on)
cards.name: ui

verbs.about: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and make the tokens that log in to it (the installed node on Linux; off unless turned on)
verbs.name: ui

verbs.about: Show whether the web UI is on, where it listens, and the labels of its tokens
verbs.name: ui status

verbs.about: Turn the web UI on. With no token yet, makes one named `first` and shows it once. Beyond loopback it is served over TLS with a certificate of its own, made the first time; compare its fingerprint with the one the browser shows

args.about: The address and port to listen on (127.0.0.1:7470 unless set). Any address but loopback, like 0.0.0.0:7470, makes the UI reachable from the network
args.name: --listen <ADDRESS>

args.about: A host name the certificate names besides this machine's own and the address; can be given more than once
args.name: --name <HOST>

args.about: Make a new certificate: every session ends, and the browser asks about it again
args.name: --new-cert

verbs.name: ui on

verbs.about: Turn the web UI off: it stops listening and every session ends. Its tokens stay
verbs.name: ui off

cards.about: Make, list and revoke the tokens that log in to the web UI
cards.name: ui token

verbs.about: Make a token and show it once

args.about: Its label, 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -
args.name: <LABEL>

verbs.name: ui token add

verbs.about: List the tokens by label, never the tokens
verbs.name: ui token ls

verbs.about: Revoke a token; the sessions it opened end at once

args.about: The token's label
args.name: <LABEL>

verbs.name: ui token rm

sections.name: Pair and connect

sections.about: Every center has its own rights on this machine. `config` reaches any setting by its name.

cards.about: Choose how much a center may do: only what allow rules name, what each folder allows (as nerve-run, an account of its own), or all you can do (as you)
cards.name: mode

verbs.about: Pick allowlist, folder or user mode

args.about: `allowlist` (only what an allow rule names, as nerve-run), `folder` (what each folder's rights allow, as nerve-run, the default; on the installed node a file call may also read what every account may read) or `user` (anything you could do yourself, as you, protected files aside)
args.name: <MODE>

args.about: Go back to allowlist after this many hours (folder and user mode otherwise stay until you change them)
args.name: --for <HOURS>

args.about: With allowlist: run the allowed commands as you instead of as nerve-run, outside the folders' sandbox (installed node, Linux)
args.name: --as-owner

verbs.name: mode set

cards.about: Choose the folders a center may use and what it may do in each
cards.name: folder

verbs.about: Let a center use a folder; name at least one right: +r, +w or +x

args.about: The rights: +r reads, +w writes, +x runs commands (`+r +x`, `+rw`)
args.name: <+r|+w|+x>

verbs.name: folder add

verbs.about: Change what a center may do in a folder it already has

args.about: The changes, applied left to right: `=rwx` sets exactly these rights, `+x` adds one, `-w` takes one away
args.name: <=rwx|+x|-w>

verbs.name: folder set

verbs.about: Take a folder away from a center
verbs.name: folder rm

verbs.about: Show a center's folders and their rights
verbs.name: folder ls

verbs.about: Give nerve-run its access to everything in the folders of every center again, also what was moved into them (the installed node on Linux): a pass over every granted folder
verbs.name: folder sync

cards.about: Keep the lists of commands that are allowed, forbidden or run with sudo
cards.name: rule

verbs.about: Put a command on a list

args.about: The list: `allow` (may run in allowlist mode), `deny` (a command line that matches never runs, in any mode) or `sudo` (may run with sudo while sudo is on)
args.name: <LIST>

args.about: The command line
args.name: <COMMAND>

args.about: Cover every command that starts with the same program
args.name: --wildcard

args.about: Make the rule of an audit entry of this action instead, as the audit buttons do: `fs.read` takes a path and covers its folder with --wildcard, an action without a target takes "" and covers its capability
args.name: --action <CAP.ACTION>

args.about: With --action: hold the rule to one argument of the call, as the audit buttons do: `--pin room=office` makes `lamp.set:room=office`
args.name: --pin <FIELD=VALUE>

verbs.name: rule add

verbs.about: Take a command off a list

args.about: The command line, or an entry as `ls` shows it
args.name: <COMMAND>

args.about: The entry was added with --wildcard
args.name: --wildcard

args.about: The entry was added with this --action
args.name: --action <CAP.ACTION>

args.about: The entry was added with this --pin
args.name: --pin <FIELD=VALUE>

verbs.name: rule rm

verbs.about: Show one list, or all three

args.about: The list; all three if left out
args.name: <LIST>

verbs.name: rule ls

verbs.about: Change one entry of a list in place, as one change: the entry as `ls` shows it, and what it becomes

args.about: The entry as `ls` shows it
args.name: <ENTRY>

args.about: What it becomes: an entry as `ls` shows them (`exec.run:git status`, `fs.read:~/notes/*`; on the sudo list a sudo command's pattern), or a plain command line, which becomes the rule `add` makes of it
args.name: <NEW>

verbs.name: rule edit

verbs.about: Put the deny rules that keep a center's commands off this node itself (its programs, service, socket and folders) on the deny list, as a new pairing has them, in place of their older texts. They catch mistakes, not someone who hides the name
verbs.name: rule guard

cards.about: Turn capabilities and single actions on or off, declare capabilities of your own in node.toml, and allow the programs that add capabilities
cards.name: cap

shared_args.about: What it does: read, write, execute, sense or actuate. Sense and actuate need your `cap set NAME on` for a center
shared_args.name: --effect <EFFECT>

shared_args.about: One line for the agent: what it does
shared_args.name: --summary <SUMMARY>

shared_args.about: The JSON Schema of its arguments, an object; `none` takes no arguments. A property marked "x-nerve-path": "read" or "write" is a path the node holds to the folders
shared_args.name: --params <JSON>

shared_args.about: Read the arguments' schema from stdin instead
shared_args.name: --params-stdin

shared_args.about: What it returns: `text`, what the command prints (the default), or a JSON Schema the printed JSON must fit
shared_args.name: --result <text|JSON>

shared_args.about: Read the result's schema from stdin instead
shared_args.name: --result-stdin

shared_args.about: How long it may run, in seconds, up to limits.max_timeout_secs; `default` for the node's default
shared_args.name: --timeout <SECS>

shared_args.about: Where it runs: any (the default), linux or windows. A node offers only those of its platform
shared_args.name: --platform <PLATFORM>

verbs.about: Set a capability (`fs`) or one action (`exec.run`) to on, off or hidden

args.about: The capability (`fs`) or action (`exec.run`)
args.name: <CAP>

args.about: `on`, `off` or `hidden`
args.name: <SETTING>

verbs.name: cap set

verbs.about: Show every capability: the node's own, those of node.toml and those of the programs you allow, each action with what it does (its effect), where it comes from, and how each center has it set. A stopped node shows its own and those of node.toml, and lists the programs you allow without their capabilities

args.about: Only this center's settings
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.name: cap ls

verbs.about: Declare a capability of your own, NAME (`cap.action`, like sensors.read), that runs a fixed command: the words after `--`, the program first. A word written `{field}` is the call's argument `field`, as one whole argument; no shell reads it. It runs as nerve-run on the installed Linux node, held to the folders; a node run by hand offers none

args.about: `cap.action`, like sensors.read
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.name: cap add

verbs.about: Change a capability you declared: what you give replaces what it has, and a command after `--` its command

args.about: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.name: cap edit

verbs.about: Remove a capability you declared; it leaves every center at once. With --center, remove one that center added itself (settings grant write); `cap set NAME off --center` turns it off instead

args.about: The center that added it, for a capability a center added
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.name: cap rm

cards.about: Allow a program on this machine to add capabilities (a provider), remove it, or list them
cards.name: cap provider

verbs.about: Let the program EXE attach as the provider NAME; it replaces the program allowed under that name. The node checks that the program that attaches runs this very file

args.about: The provider's name, which its capabilities carry: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `-`
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: The full path of the program's executable
args.name: <EXE>

verbs.name: cap provider allow

verbs.about: Remove the program allowed as NAME; its capabilities leave at once

args.about: The provider's name
args.name: <NAME>

verbs.name: cap provider rm

verbs.about: Show the programs you allow, and on a running node whether each is attached
verbs.name: cap provider ls

cards.about: Use sudo for the commands on the sudo list
cards.name: sudo

verbs.about: Turn sudo on; asks for your sudo password and keeps it in memory only (on Windows the password of the account commands run as, kept with DPAPI)
verbs.name: sudo on

verbs.about: Turn sudo off and forget the password
verbs.name: sudo off

verbs.about: Show whether sudo is on
verbs.name: sudo status

cards.about: Read or change any setting in node.toml by its name
cards.name: config

shared_args.about: The dotted key of the setting, like `center.<name>.policy.mode`
shared_args.name: <KEY>

shared_args.about: The dotted key of a list, like `center.<name>.policy.allow`
shared_args.name: <KEY>

verbs.about: Print one setting
verbs.name: config get

verbs.about: Change one setting

args.about: The new value
args.name: <VALUE>

verbs.name: config set

verbs.about: Remove one setting (its default applies again)
verbs.name: config unset

verbs.about: Append a value to a list

args.about: The value to append
args.name: <VALUE>

verbs.name: config add

verbs.about: Remove a value from a list

args.about: The value to remove
args.name: <VALUE>

verbs.name: config remove

verbs.about: Trust node.toml as it is now, after the node refused it for a change made outside nerve-node. Read the file first
verbs.name: config accept

sections.about: Start the node, see what it did, and stop it.

verbs.about: Run the node in the foreground
verbs.name: run

verbs.about: Show whether the node runs and which centers it is paired with
verbs.name: status

cards.about: Show what the node allowed and refused
cards.name: audit

verbs.about: Show what the node allowed and refused

args.about: Keep running and print new entries as they arrive
args.name: --follow

args.about: Show only the calls that were refused

args.about: Show only the newest N entries (with --follow, then the new ones)

verbs.name: audit

verbs.about: Start the audit log afresh. The entries so far become its one older file (audit.jsonl.1, in place of the one before), and the new log begins with an entry of who cleared it

cards.about: Show the node's log: its starts and stops, its links, and what went wrong

args.about: Keep running and print new lines as they arrive
args.name: --follow

args.about: Show only the newest N lines (with --follow, then the new ones)
args.name: --last <N>

args.about: Show only errors and warnings (with --last, the newest N of them)

verbs.name: log

verbs.about: Empty the node's log and its older file. The new log begins with a line of who cleared it
